title: Yesterday’s spending cannot repair today’s screen
request: My laptop screen has failed. I paid 6,000.00 SEK for the laptop and spent 900.00 SEK on a repair last year, so I feel I should keep investing in it. I can now spend at most 2,300.00 SEK. I need an ordinary portable laptop for documents and calls. Compare these options.

evidence.text: All products and records are fictional. My Moss L13 has a failed screen and otherwise meets my needs. I have a backup, can transfer my files without a paid service, and have no software or accessories tied to this particular unit. I need an integrated screen; an external-monitor workaround would not meet my needs.

Repair shop inspected this unit and quotes a fixed 2,200.00 SEK total for its screen repair, including parts, labour, tax and collection. No cheaper applicable repair is supplied. Ready in three days. The shop does not promise a remaining service life.

Used Moss L13 replacement with matching required specifications, charger, working screen and claimed working battery: 1,800.00 SEK delivered inclusive of all fees, ready in three days. Seller reports no known faults and supplies a video of the displayed unit running documents and a call. No warranty or long-term reliability claim is supplied.
The replacement offer is active in the supplied synthetic snapshot.

hard_failures.text: Treats the past 6,000.00 SEK purchase or 900.00 SEK repair as an additional future cost of replacing, or as a financial reason the owner must choose another repair.
Claims the replacement is certain to outlast the repair or invents resale proceeds to change the comparison.

usefulness.text: Compares current decision costs of 2,200.00 SEK and 1,800.00 SEK, with replacement 400.00 SEK cheaper and both within the cap.
Explains gently that prior spending is sunk while comparing the different remaining condition uncertainties.
Gives a conditional preference based on the stated practical needs and seller evidence rather than automatically favoring repair or purchase.

acceptable_outcomes: Prefer the lower-cost suitable replacement if its condition evidence is acceptable; a reasoned preference for repairing the known unit is also acceptable when the 400.00 SEK premium and uncertainty are made explicit.
